about: A preview of the BBC Micro's registry record as it will be once the machine counts as running, for builds that test its page before then: tests/bbc-page.test.mjs and scripts/browser-check.mjs build the site with REGISTRY_PREVIEW set to this file, and nothing that deploys does. status, acceptance, rights and notes are the record as it will be; copy them into machines/registry.json when the BBC Micro is switched on, then delete this file. photos is a stand-in, the KIM-1's photograph, only because a running machine must have one and the BBC Micro's is not chosen yet; it is never published, and it is not copied.

bbc-micro.rights: The three ROMs are Acorn's: the operating system, MOS 1.20, BBC BASIC 2 and the Disc Filing System, DFS 1.20. The operating system's own text says copyright 1981 Acorn Computers Ltd. and BASIC's copyright 1982 Acorn. Who holds that copyright now was not established, and no licence or permission from any holder was found. Our copies are from jsbeeb's ROM folder at a pinned commit, kept in this repository under roms/, with where they came from, and checked by SHA-256 each time they are read. The position is documented, not cleared: if a rights holder asks, the ROMs will be removed.
bbc-micro.notes: The keyboard, the picture in all eight screen modes, teletext included, the sound chip, and the disc drive with Acorn's DFS, on MOS 1.20 and BBC BASIC 2. Not modelled: the serial port, the analogue port, the Tube, the cassette interface, the printer port and the 1 MHz bus.

photos.author: Rama & Musée Bolo, cropped by Tomer T
photos.caption: an original MOS Technology KIM-1, on display at the Musée Bolo, EPFL, Lausanne
photos.alt: An original KIM-1 board seen from directly above on a black background: a dark green circuit board with gold edge contacts on two tabs down its left side, three 40-pin chips at the top left, a column of eight memory chips, a crystal and the KIM-1 name at the top right, the six-digit display behind a dark filter, and the black keypad of 23 keys with its SST switch at the bottom right.
photos.used: the tracks on the top face, as one of three photographs of it; the keypad's size and its keys' places, the display window, the crystal, the name and the red wire; and a check on where the chips sit
